name.text: Is the trapezoidal estimate too big or too small

questiontext.text:

Graph C: [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt1]]

[[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Graph [[if test="is(pU=1)"]]A[[elif test="is(pU=2)"]]B[[else]]C[[/if]] bends upwards, like a bowl: the straight tops (chords) lie above the curve, so each trapezium includes extra area and the estimate is an overestimate.

Graph [[if test="is(pD=1)"]]A[[elif test="is(pD=2)"]]B[[else]]C[[/if]] bends downwards, like an arch: the chords lie below the curve, so some area is left out and the estimate is an underestimate.

The remaining graph is a straight line: the top of each trapezium lies along it, so the estimate is exact.

Chords lie above a curve that bends upwards, so trapezia overestimate. The strips are all the same width; the error comes only from the straight tops.

questiondescription.text:
Area Approximations: is the trapezoidal estimate too big or too small

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.2 (b) / Essential 2.1 (b): Decide from three graphs whether the trapezoidal estimate is an overestimate, an underestimate or exact, and give the reason for an overestimate.

Core and Essential

This question is adapted from Question C1 in Section C of Chapter 9 of Cassell, D., Instone, S., Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP AS/A2 Mathematics: Core 2 for AQA, Cambridge University Press, 2004: deciding too large or too small from a diagram, as three graphs (bowl, arch, straight line) in a random order, with the reason as a choice.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core and Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).
